newsitem.title: CANADA: Lebanon says Netanyahu fostering Arab extremists.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon says Netanyahu fostering Arab extremists.

text.p: Lebanese Prime Minister Rafik al-Hariri charged on Thursday that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's tough policies were fostering the growth of fundamentalist groups like Hamas and Hizbollah.
He said the Israelis insisted on maintaining a security zone in southern Lebanon to protect against the Shiite Moslem group Hizbollah.
"But in fact, Hizbollah exists because they (Israelis) are there, and they are strengthening Hizbollah in reality," Hariri told a joint foreign affairs committee in the Canadian Parliament.
"As well, by blocking the (Middle East) peace process, they are strengthening Hamas, which is the Islamic fundamentalist (group)."

Hariri asked: "What is the situation of (Palestinian President) Yasser Arafat? He is weakening. Who is weakening him? Netanyahu. Who is getting stronger now among the Palestinians? The fundamentalists."
He said the Israeli leader was doing the same in Morocco, Egypt, Jordan and throughout the region: "This is wrong. This is absolutely wrong."
Hariri, on the first visit of a Lebanese prime minister to Canada, met Prime Minister Jean Chretien on Thursday morning and said Chretien accepted an invitation to come to Lebanon.
Hariri, a rich businessman who personally bankrolled part of the restoration of Beirut's city core after years of war, also said he hoped for a free-trade arrangement with Canada.

"We are discussing with the European Union the signing of a free trade agreement with Europe...We don't want to make it only with Europe," he said, adding that it would be good to establish similar deals with Canada.
Canada and Israel implemented a free-trade agreement at the start of this year.
